# synthetic { #wdm.synthetic }

`synthetic`

Synthetic data generation, for testing and for calibrating expectations.

Two distinct uses.

**Validation.** Parameter recovery on data generated from known parameters is
the only way to know whether the estimator works. Real data has no ground truth,
so a plausible-looking fit there proves nothing at all.

**Power analysis.** Before you spend four months logging, it is worth knowing
what four months of data can actually resolve. Generating synthetic episodes of
varying length and logging quality, then looking at how wide the posteriors come
out, answers that honestly -- and the answer for some parameters is "not much".
Better to learn that from a simulation than from a spreadsheet in December.

## Classes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [SyntheticSpec](#wdm.synthetic.SyntheticSpec) | Configuration for one synthetic episode. |

### SyntheticSpec { #wdm.synthetic.SyntheticSpec }

```python
synthetic.SyntheticSpec(
    n_days=120,
    start_weight_kg=100.0,
    body_fat_frac=0.3,
    intake_fraction=0.8,
    intake_sd_kcal=250.0,
    protein_g_per_kg=1.8,
    fat_fraction_of_kcal=0.3,
    carb_weekly_amplitude_g=60.0,
    obs_sd_kg=0.45,
    weigh_in_rate=0.85,
    logging_rate=0.9,
    sodium_mean_mg=3000.0,
    sodium_sd_mg=800.0,
    include_sodium=True,
    habitual_carb_g=None,
    habitual_sodium_mg=None,
    waist_every_days=0,
    waist_offset_cm=75.0,
    waist_slope_cm_per_kg=1.2,
    waist_sd_cm=1.5,
)
```

Configuration for one synthetic episode.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [make_episode](#wdm.synthetic.make_episode) | Simulate one episode and return it alongside the hidden ground truth. |
| [make_weight_only_episode](#wdm.synthetic.make_weight_only_episode) | A past episode with weigh-ins but no food log, mimicking old history. |

### make_episode { #wdm.synthetic.make_episode }

```python
synthetic.make_episode(
    spec,
    true_params,
    *,
    name='synthetic',
    start_date='2026-01-01',
    seed=0,
    noise=None,
)
```

Simulate one episode and return it alongside the hidden ground truth.

The simulation runs the *same* dynamics the estimator uses, which makes this
a test of the estimator rather than of the model. That is the correct scope:
whether the model resembles human physiology is a question for the
literature and for residual diagnostics on real data, not for a self-test.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                     |
|--------|---------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | episode | An `~wdm.io.Episode` as if loaded from a CSV.                                                                                            |
|        | truth   | Dict of the hidden trajectories: ``tissue_kg``, ``fat_kg``, ``gly_water_kg``, ``na_water_kg``, ``adapt_kcal``, and the noise-free ``scale_kg``. |

### make_weight_only_episode { #wdm.synthetic.make_weight_only_episode }

```python
synthetic.make_weight_only_episode(spec, true_params, *, name, start_date, seed)
```

A past episode with weigh-ins but no food log, mimicking old history.
